title: Stay-History Courtesy on Room Reservations No-Show Charges
content:
**The courtesy.** On a no-show charge on a Room Reservations reservation, a guest whose Ashbury Rewards account shows at least 6 stays credited in the twelve months before the day of handling, each stay night-credit posting counting as one stay whatever its nights and a posting dated on or before the same calendar date twelve months earlier being outside them, has the steady-guest courtesy of 10% taken off; one whose account shows at least 4 such stays has the repeat-guest courtesy of 5% taken off; any other guest has no stay courtesy (0%).

**Q. Which postings are stays?**
Night-credit postings for stay nights on the guest's Ashbury Rewards account. Each such posting is one stay, whether it credited one night or ten.

**Q. Where does the twelve-month window start?**
On the day after the same calendar date twelve months before the day of handling: a posting dated on that same date, or earlier, is outside the window. With a hypothetical day of handling of 15 March 2027, a posting of 16 March 2026 counts and one of 15 March 2026 does not.

**Q. How do the counts map to the courtesy?**

| Stays counted | Courtesy |
|---|---|
| 6 or more | 10% |
| 4 or 5 | 5% |
| 3 or fewer | none |

**Q. Where does the courtesy act?**
It takes its share off the no-show charge as it stands at that point, before the charge is rounded.

**Q. What does 5% come to?**
On a hypothetical charge of 198.00 standing before the courtesy, a guest with 4 stays counted is charged 188.10; one with 6 stays, 178.20; one with 3 stays, 198.00.
